title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
claim: Intermediate representations are already predictive, but the original decoder's performance jumps abruptly at specific depths, revealing distinct inference stages.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared x-axis and legend below, shaded bands
description: Two side-by-side line plots share a y-axis labeled Performance (0.5 to 1.0) and an x-axis labeled Layers in forward-pass order. The left panel is titled TabPFN(2.5) and the right is titled LIMIX-16M. Each panel has four curves with shaded variance bands. Blue lines are the original decoder: solid for ROC-AUC and dashed for balanced accuracy. Orange lines are individually trained decoders, with the same solid and dashed coding. The orange curves jump early, within the first few layers, then plateau near 1.0. The blue curves stay low, then rise in sudden steps at later layers, and the dashed blue curve dips and recovers along the way. All curves converge near 1.0 at the final layer. A two-column legend sits below the plots. The eye goes first to the steep orange rise and the lagging blue curves.
caption: Individually trained decoders (–, - -) exhibit good performance early, showing that representations are descriptive but not aligned with the original decoder. For the original decoder, the sudden increase in ROC-AUC (–) and balanced accuracy (- -) at different layers suggests inference stages.
abstract: Transformer-based tabular foundation models (TFMs) dominate small to medium tabular predictive benchmark tasks, yet their inference mechanisms remain largely unexplored. We present the first large-scale mechanistic study of layerwise dynamics in 6 state-of-the-art tabular in-context learning models. We explore how predictions emerge across depth, identify distinct stages of inference and reveal latent-space dynamics that differ from those of language models. Our findings indicate substantial depthwise redundancy across multiple models, suggesting iterative refinement with overlapping computations during inference stages. Guided by these insights, we design a proof-of-concept, looped single-layer model that uses only 20% of the original model's parameters while achieving comparable performance. The code is available at https://github.com/amirbalef/is_one_layer_enough.
